cues.en: It's the early hours of the morning, the sun is rising, I'm 32% caffeine by volume.
cues.zh: 现在是凌晨，太阳正在升起，我体内咖啡因的占比达到了32%。

cues.en: So, it's time for another Minute Medicine. This one's actually inspired by a patient I spoke to tonight who asked a very interesting question, which I think is often dismissed as simplistic because it's got an obvious initial answer and I don't think people take the thought process any further. But it's actually a very thought provoking question. And the question is, when we don't know what's going on with a patient, why don't we just test them for everything?
cues.zh: 好了，又到了《一分钟医学》时间。今晚我和一位患者聊过，他问了一个很有意思的问题，这次的内容就由此启发而来。这个问题常被人当成很简单，因为乍一看答案显而易见，而大家似乎也不会继续往下想。但它其实很值得深思。问题是：当我们不知道患者出了什么问题时，为什么不干脆给他们做所有检查？

cues.en: And the obvious answer, which makes most people dismiss it, is that it would cost too much and be impractical. But the patient who asked me is actually a real life multimillionaire
cues.zh: 显而易见的答案，也是大多数人直接否定它的原因，就是太贵而且不切实际。但问我这个问题的病人，其实是个如假包换的千万富翁，

cues.en: and he asked me in a purely hypothetical sense if he was willing to pay for every test we had in our armament,
cues.zh: 他纯粹是做个假设，问我如果他愿意自费做我们掌握的所有检查，

cues.en: why don't we just send them all off? I actually got thinking about it and realised it's an interesting question.
cues.zh: 为什么不干脆全做一遍呢？我仔细琢磨了一下，发现这还真是个有意思的问题。

cues.en: Every test has a false positive and false negative rate. A false positive is where a patient doesn't have a disease, but the test says that he or she does. And a false negative is the opposite is where a patient does have the disease, a test says that they don't. Now, let's say a test has a false positive rate of one in a thousand. In the real world, we'd say that's quite a good test. And if we imagine we're testing for the crippling disease
cues.zh: 每个检测都有假阳性和假阴性率。假阳性是指患者没有病，但检测却说他或她有病。假阴性则相反，是患者确实有病，检测却说没有。假设一个检测的假阳性率是千分之一。在现实世界里，我们会说这检测相当不错了。再设想我们要检测的是一种致残疾病

cues.en: which makes you lose your hair and all your joints turn to wood, and rhodinitis affects the population at a rate of one in one thousand.
cues.zh: 它会让你掉光头发、所有关节都变成木头一样僵硬，而鼻炎性病变在人群中的发病率是千分之一。

cues.en: If I test the next one thousand patients to walk through my hospital door unselected,
cues.zh: 如果我接下来检测一千名不经筛选、走进我医院的患者，

cues.en: predict that a false positive rate of one in a thousand will give one false positive for those one thousand people, but would also expect one sufferer in those one thousand people. So, if I get one positive test, there's a fiftyfifty chance that it's wrong, and that's rubbish. Now, imagine rhogenitis affects the population at a rate of one in ten thousand, and I test the next ten thousand people to walk through the door with a test that has a false positive rate of one in a thousand,
cues.zh: 如果假阳性率是千分之一，这一千人里预计会出现一个假阳性；同时，我们也预计其中有一名患者确实患病。所以，如果我拿到一个阳性结果，它有一半的可能是错的，这毫无用处。现在，假设鼻炎在人群中的发病率是万分之一，我用假阳性率为千分之一的检测，检查接下来走进医院的这一万人，

cues.en: then for every ten positive results,
cues.zh: 那么每十个阳性结果里，

cues.en: and that's clearly completely useless. And we haven't even started to factor in false negatives into this equation. So you can quickly see how pretest probability
cues.zh: 这显然完全没用。而且，我们还没把假阴性纳入这个计算。所以你很快就能看出，检测前概率……

cues.en: is such an important concept in medicine. You have to narrow down which tests you send for which patient and you do this with old fashioned techniques like talking to the patient and examining them. So, if your doctor doesn't want to run a particular test on you, it doesn't mean that she's trying to save money or anything like that, but she has to have a reasonable suspicion
cues.zh: 在医学中是个极其重要的概念。你得缩小检查范围，确定给哪位病人做哪项检查，而这靠的是传统方法，比如和病人交流以及做体检。所以，如果你的医生不想给你做某项特定检查，并不意味着她在省钱或怎么着，而是她必须有合理的怀疑，

cues.en: that you may have a given diagnosis before running a test in order to get an interpretable result. And remember, some tests also have risks that may be very small, like a bit of radiation from a CT scan, but if we start running every test on every patient, these quickly add up. Now, I'm off to be passive aggressive at the morning handover and to get some more coffee, and yes, I drink out of a glass because I'm fancy,
cues.zh: 认为你可能患有某种疾病，然后再做检查，这样结果才有参考价值。别忘了，有些检查也有风险，哪怕风险很小，比如 CT 扫描的一点点辐射，但如果我们给每个病人都做所有检查，这些风险很快就会累积起来。好了，我现在要去早交班上搞点阴阳怪气了，顺便再搞点咖啡，没错，我用玻璃杯喝，因为我讲究，
